newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB grain railcar allocations to be set by region.
newsitem.headline: CWB grain railcar allocations to be set by region.

text.p: The assignment of hopper cars carrying Canadian Wheat Board wheat and barley will be done by region rather than "train-runs" starting in January, said Greg Arason, chairman of the Car Allocation Policy Group (CAPG).
The move is part of long-term reforms to move Canadian freight markets into more orderly commercial patterns, Arason said in remarks to a meeting of the Canada Grains Council.

"Further down the road, another number of changes will be examined. These include allocating a portion of cars on advance orders and the balance of available car supply on the basis of shipper demand patterns," Arason said.
Arason said car allocations of CWB grains will cover 27 zones in the first year, each containing six to 10 train runs.
Canada abolished its federal rail car allocation agency and its C$561 million annual rail subsidies for farmers on August 1, 1995, to comply with world trade agreements.

The CAPG, an industry group, has stepped in to oversee the transition of freight to free market structures by the year 2000, when its mandate and federally regulated maximum rail freight rates will be reviewed.
"This puts us in a position to reduce the need for buffer stocks and it means managing our assets more efficiently," Arason said.
CWB grain accounts for 81 percent of grain railcar unloadings at Vancouver and Port Rupert and 70 percent at Thunder Bay. (Winnipeg bureau 204 947 3548)
